migration.description: Introduce a durable prompt-cache conversation master and compact proxy invocation identity allocation, then add the additive latest-success route lookup index used by online routing checks.
migration.release_unit_description: Prompt-cache conversation background materialization follow-up for the conversation and invoke ID redesign.

durable_state.description: Prompt-cache conversation identity rows and delayed aggregate statistics derived from retained proxy invocations, with a durable refresh queue, freshness markers, and resumable phase/cursor state for background materialization; pool_upstream_request_attempts also has an additive partial success lookup index.
durable_state.storage_implementation: SQLite prompt_cache_conversations table, prompt_cache_conversation_stats_refresh_queue table, prompt_cache_conversation_migration_progress table, prompt_cache_conversation_materialization_runs table, codex_invocations mutation triggers, maintenance-database managed_tasks and startup_backfill_progress control/checkpoint rows, the additive maintenance_metadata prompt_cache_materialization_control_origin_v1 marker, schema_refresh_migrations markers for identity backfill and aggregate-statistics freshness, and idx_pool_attempts_account_model_success. No table or column is added by the control-consistency repair. The trigger-dependency repair replaces existing working-set trigger definitions and adds only the prompt_cache_working_set_relevant_updates_v1 completion row in schema_refresh_migrations.

ddl_structural_changes.description: Create prompt_cache_conversations, its constraints, and lookup indexes.
Create the durable prompt-cache statistics refresh queue and codex_invocations mutation triggers that enqueue affected keys and invalidate freshness.

Create the additive migration progress table with migration_name, phase, source_max_invocation_id, cursor_key, completed_keys, updated_at, and the durable source total so materialization can resume after cancellation or restart and expose bounded progress.
Create the bounded materialization run history table for phase, duration, processed/updated counts, batch metrics, defer reasons, and failures; retain only the latest 100 rows.

Create idx_pool_attempts_account_model_success on (upstream_account_id, request_model COLLATE NOCASE, id DESC, started_at) for status='success' using idempotent startup DDL; index construction is timed and can be re-entered after interruption without converting business rows.

Replace existing Prompt live working-set triggers with an UPDATE OF dependency guard; commit DDL and the prompt_cache_working_set_relevant_updates_v1 completion marker atomically. Existing initialized projections receive no row rebuild, and an interrupted marker write rolls back all trigger changes for safe startup retry.

dml_changes.description: Before task-registry seeding, record whether the prompt-cache managed task row already exists. Existing maintenance control remains authoritative; the legacy business enabled bit can seed the managed control once only when that row was absent.

In the background identity_backfill phase, snapshot the maximum invocation ID and materialize distinct historical prompt-cache keys by keyset pages; after the snapshot scan, run uncursored missing-identity reconciliation and record the identity marker only after coverage is complete.

After identity coverage is complete, stats_rebuild traverses conversation keys and stages bounded 256-invocation pages. Only a generation-consistent final page publishes an aggregate and clears that queue generation; the outer key cursor advances after all required statistics are complete.

In the background queue_drain phase, refresh and clear durable mutation-queue keys only after successful aggregate refresh, then record the statistics freshness marker and complete phase when the queue is empty.

progress_signals: The prompt_cache_conversation_migration_progress row exposes the current phase, invocation snapshot boundary, keyset cursor, committed identity-key counter, and updated_at checkpoint; schema setup repairs counters for older complete rows.

The system prompt-cache materialization status surface exposes total keys, completed keys, progress, queue backlog, estimated remaining time, the latest 10 bounded run records, and the maintenance-database pause/resume control; the legacy business-database enabled value is retained and can seed a newly created managed control once, but is ignored after initialization.

The maintenance_metadata prompt_cache_materialization_control_origin_v1 marker preserves an existing maintenance task control across upgrade and records whether one-time legacy initialization is applicable; older programs can ignore the additive metadata row.

Structured startup-backfill logs expose phase, scanned, updated, completion, retry, failure, and defer status, together with micro-batch count, last/max batch size, accumulated batch time, and defer reason; failed prompt-cache records retain the durable phase checkpoint.
Structured identity creation, collision retry, database recovery, statistics refresh, and retention release logs.

The prompt_cache_conversations_stats_v2 marker identifies a completed aggregate refresh only when the prompt_cache_conversation_stats_refresh_queue is empty; its absence or a pending queue triggers a paged startup rebuild.

The latest-success route lookup index is additive, partial on status='success', timed during startup creation, and recreated idempotently after interruption; older readers continue to use the unchanged attempt rows.

Startup logs the committed working-set trigger refresh marker and elapsed time. Repeated startup skips this completed trigger-only upgrade; existing projection rows and unrelated migration markers remain unchanged.
pause_points: Schema installation stops after additive DDL and does not scan historical invocations, allowing HTTP readiness to continue.

The operator control commits managed_tasks.enabled and its maintenance scheduler checkpoint together, then publishes the in-process generation. Disable stops new short SQL steps at the next boundary while an already registered step may finish; re-enable wakes from the durable business cursor.

Identity discovery commits adaptive 32..400-key identity batches with their cursor and counter. Statistics pages commit bounded staging progress separately; only complete aggregates advance the outer statistics cursor. A committed boundary may yield to priority or pause, and a process restart repeats only idempotent work. Completed pages and empty phase transitions use the remaining run budget; incomplete pages retain the 15-second follow-up.

SQLite invocation mutation triggers enqueue affected prompt-cache keys and remove the freshness marker in the source transaction; startup recovery can rebuild aggregates and identities after a stopped release.

required_test_evidence: Schema installation completes without scanning historical prompt-cache invocations.
A bounded startup materialization creates identities, checkpoints committed pages, and reruns without duplicate identities.

Adaptive identity batches commit identities and their cursor together; bounded statistics pages retain staging progress, publish only complete generation-consistent aggregates, and yield only at committed boundaries.
A stopped release or process restart resumes from the durable phase/cursor and converges to both markers with an empty queue.

Independent business and maintenance databases prove that an existing maintenance control wins when the legacy business enable bit disagrees, while a legacy-only database can seed a newly created managed control once; later execution follows only maintenance managed_tasks.enabled and never synchronizes the legacy bit.

A statistics key requiring multiple source pages retains committed staging progress, reports a typed defer reason, and resumes without advancing the outer cursor or publishing a premature freshness marker.
An invocation payload update enqueues its prompt-cache key and startup recovery creates the missing identity before rebuilding aggregates.
Aggregate reads return the existing unavailable contract while identity, statistics, or queue completeness is not satisfied.
A cache miss recovers the next sequence from retained invocation IDs.
Retention releases orphan masters without a permanent ID blacklist.

The production terminal timing write does not recompute the live working set. Relevant mutations match a source rebuild; a failed completion-marker insertion rolls back legacy trigger replacement, and successful/repeated startup preserves live rows. Older service readers accept the unchanged tables and additive marker.
